ukmt-stmc-2019-20-final-crossnumber-01.title: Work through the clues
ukmt-stmc-2019-20-final-crossnumber-01.body:
(The published paper has no answers; this solution was worked out and checked against every clue.)

**Clues that stand alone.** 6A: $256^{100}\times625^{200}=2^{800}\cdot5^{800}=10^{800}$, which has $800$ zeroes. 11A: NEWTON has $6$ letters with N twice, so $\frac{6!}{2!}=360$. 19A $=15^2-14=211$. 2D $=400-20=380$. 18D: HYPATIA has $7$ letters with A twice: $\frac{7!}{2!}=2520$. 22D: $512^{16}\times125^{48}=2^{144}\cdot5^{144}=10^{144}$, which has $145$ digits. 9D: one-eighth of $360$ is $45$ and $\sqrt{108^2+45^2}=117$. 5D: a polygon with $800$ sides has angle sum $798\cdot180$, and one twentieth of it is $7182$. 13A: with $145$ sides, $\frac{143\cdot180}{10}=2574$.

**Using those.** 10A $=800+117=917$. 17D: $\frac{17D+145}2=211$, so 17D $=277$. 1A: $5x+6y=380$ and $2x+y=145$ give $x=70$, so 1A $=123$. 19D: with 11A $=360$, $n^2-37n-360=0$ has positive solution $n=45$; an even three-digit multiple of $45$ is a multiple of $90$, and 19D starts with $2$ (the first digit of 19A), so it is $270$. 12D and 25A: 25A is a three-digit factor of $2520$ and 12D $=\frac54\cdot$25A, a three-digit number starting with $6$ (the middle digit of 11A), so $600\le\frac54\cdot25A<700$, i.e. $480\le25A<560$. The only factor of $2520$ in that range is $504$, so 25A $=504$ and 12D $=630$.

**Fibonacci clues.** 3D has five digits: $10946,17711,28657,46368,75025$. Its second digit is the last digit of 6A, $0$, so 3D $=10946$. 3A starts with the first digit of 3D, so it is $1597$. Then 15D $=1597+10946=12543$. 20D: $19x+4y=211$ and $7x+6y=123$ give $x=9$, $y=10$, so 20D $=1597-10=1587$. 8A $=1587-277=1310$. 24A $=\frac{10946+2520}2=6733$.

**Remaining clues via crossings.** 4D is a multiple of $211$ whose first digit is $9$ (the third digit of 3A) and third digit is $7$ (the last digit of 10A): $9073=211\cdot43$. 23A $=4?4$ (crossing 15D and 22D) is a multiple of $4$ with 21A $=\frac54\cdot$23A ending in $5$ (crossing 15D): so 23A $=404$ or $444$; and 7D $=|23A-504|$ must have three digits, so 23A $=404$, 21A $=505$, 7D $=100$. 16A has the form $?202$ and 14D has the form $5?1$ (crossings), with 16A a multiple of $14D+100$ and $14D+100$ a factor: $1202=2\cdot601$ and $14D=501$. 22A: $m^2+17m-630=0$ has solution $m=18$, and 22A has the form $17?2$: $1782=18\cdot99$.

The completed grid satisfies all $28$ clues.
